newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B index ends down on consolidation.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B index ends down on consolidation.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index ended down slightly on Wednesday on consolidation due to concerns over company results and weakness in the domestic A share markets, but thin volume indicated sentiment was stable, brokers said.
The B share index fell 0.121 points or 0.17 percent to 73.065 points on volume of 13.9 million shares worth $6.6 million against $7.8 million on Tuesday.

The A share index consolidated down after sharp gains in the past weeks, falling 7.657 points or 0.59 percent to 1,292.738 points on turnover of eight billion yuan compared with 8.3 billion yuan on Tuesday.

Brokers said that most investors were cautious ahead of the April 30 deadline for listed companies to make public their 1996 results, but selling was also light due to fundamental investor confidence in the market.
"The correction has been expected after the recent rises and market sentiment is good despite falls in the A share market," one broker said.
"The index is likely to continue to linger around 73 points before its next run," a second broker said.
All 43 B shares traded with 26 down, three flat and 14 up.
Shanghai Shangling Electric Appliances was the biggest loser on expectations of poor 1996 results, falling $0.030 or 7.42 percent to $0.374 on volume of 393,500 shares.
Shanghai Diesel Engine traded the most on institutional selling, falling $0.010 or 2.08 percent to $0.470 on volume of 1.1 million shares.
On the A share market, the SSE30 blue chip index dipped 5.086 points or 0.15 percent to 3417.426 points.
Shanghai New Asia Fast Food lost the most on profit-taking after a financial restructuring was announced, down 8.17 percent to 13.48 yuan on volume of 1.2 million shares.
